faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella during April 2035?
faq.a: April in Marbella brings mild spring weather with air temperatures of 18–24°C and sea temperatures of 16–18°C. Expect 7–8 hours of daily sunshine and occasional short showers. Easter 2035 is on 1 April, so early April may see cooler conditions, while late April warms up nicely for cruising.

faq.q: Is it warm enough for swimming on a yacht charter in April?
faq.a: Yes, but it depends on your tolerance. The sea temperature in April averages 16–18°C, which many find refreshing. If you prefer warmer water, late April is better. Wetsuits are not provided, but the sun is strong enough to dry off quickly. Many guests enjoy a quick dip, especially on calm days.

faq.q: Which boats are best for an April charter in Puerto Banús?
faq.a: For small groups, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (both 12.5m, up to 11 pax) are excellent value from €749/2h. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski from €4,719/4h. All boats depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for Easter 2035?
faq.a: Easter week is the busiest period in Marbella. We recommend booking at least 4–6 weeks ahead, especially for larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 or Mangusta 80. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) often sell out 2–3 weeks before Easter Sunday (1 April 2035).

faq.q: What are the best routes for a spring yacht charter?

faq.q: What should I wear for a yacht charter in April?
faq.a: Dress in layers: a light jumper or jacket for the morning breeze, and shorts or swimwear for midday sun. A windbreaker is useful as sea breezes can be cool at 15–18 knots. Don't forget sunscreen (SPF 30+), sunglasses, and a hat. Non-slip shoes are recommended for boarding.

Spring brings mild air temperatures, moderate sea conditions, and fewer crowds than summer — perfect for a relaxed cruise along the Marbella coastline. Whether you're planning a family outing or a group celebration, knowing what to expect from the weather and sea can make all the difference. Here's everything you need to plan your April charter in Puerto Banús.

What's the weather like in Marbella during April 2035?

April in Marbella offers daytime air temperatures of 18–24°C, with sea temperatures hovering around 16–18°C. You can expect 7–8 hours of sunshine daily, though occasional short showers are possible, especially early in the month. Easter 2035 is on 1 April, so early April may feel slightly cooler, while late April sees warmer conditions ideal for swimming. Winds are typically moderate (10–15 knots), picking up in the afternoon. Morning departures often provide the calmest seas.

Best boats for an April charter in Puerto Banús

Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús and includes options for every group size. For small to medium groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are excellent value at €749/2h or €2,299/8h — all inclusive. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) starts at €4,719/4h and includes a free jet ski. Other boats like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Ferretti 94 are available on request. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT.

Sea conditions and sailing tips for April

The Mediterranean in April is generally calm, with wave heights of 0.5–1.5m. Afternoon breezes can create a slight chop, but our skippers know the best sheltered spots along the coast. Popular April routes include cruising east to Cabopino (20 min) or west to Cala del Faro and Estepona (45 min). If you're keen on swimming, late April offers the warmest sea temperatures. For sunset lovers, a late afternoon charter (18:00–20:00) captures the golden hour over La Concha mountain.

Easter 2035: what to expect and how to prepare

Easter Sunday 2035 is on 1 April, making it one of the earliest Easters in recent years. This means Puerto Banús will be busy, but the sea remains uncrowded compared to summer. We recommend booking 4–6 weeks in advance for larger yachts like the Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) often sell out 2–3 weeks before Easter. All charters include drinks and snacks, but you can arrange catering or a BBQ on request. Dress in layers: a light jacket for morning breezes, swimwear for midday sun.

Where to anchor and what to see in April

April is a great month to explore the Marbella coastline and nearby coves. Top spots include Cala del Faro (a quiet rocky cove near Estepona), Cala Cortés (sheltered bay with clear water), and the Río Verde area. For lunch stops, Puerto Banús itself has numerous beach clubs and restaurants. If you want a longer cruise, head to Sotogrande (1 hour west) or Málaga (1.5 hours east). Our skippers will tailor the route to your preferences.
